newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady, refinery hitches support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady, refinery hitches support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed steady on Friday after the shut-down of units at three European refineries helped the market reverse early losses.

September Brent ended one cent higher at $18.95 a barrel, having recovered from a session low of $18.63. The contract also reached a recent high and key resistance level at $19.00 in late trading but failed to break higher.
August gas oil earlier ended $2.25 a tonne firmer at $171.50.
"The stories about the cat crackers going down really gave gasoline a boost and we just came up on that," said one broker.

Two catalytic converters, one at the BP/Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam and one at the BP/Mobil Coryton refinery in the U.K. were shut down on Friday due to technical problems, taking out 115,000 barrels per day of capacity at least until the middle of next week.
In addition, Shell confirmed on Friday that the cat cracker at its Pernis refinery has closed down for an unscheduled stoppage in August followed by a scheduled stoppage of two months.
The shut downs will bolster an already bullish European gasoline market where prices have shot up by $25 a tonne over the last two weeks.
Lower production levels should also curtail exports from Europe to gasoline-thirsty United States.
Before the news of refinery disruption, Brent was languishing some 30 cents a barrel lower.
"It's tested the downside today but not really broken support," said one broker.
Some traders expect the next firm steps towards Iraqi exports could push the market lower again, but others said the news was factored into the market.
The United Nations said on Thursday that it expected approval of Iraq's aid plan, the next hurdle to a resumption of exports, by early next week.
